title: Surjectivity on morphisms from a cofibrant object to a fibrant object after localization
statement:
Let $\mathcal M$ be a complete and cocomplete ordinary category [def-nagata-category] with three classes $C,F,W$ forming a model structure: $W$ is retract closed and satisfies two-out-of-three, and $(C,F\cap W)$ and $(C\cap W,F)$ are weak factorization systems, meaning that every arrow factors into the indicated classes and each class is characterized by lifting against the other. Trivial means also in $W$. Let $L:\mathcal M\to H$ be an ordinary categorical localization at $W$: precomposition by $L$ gives an equivalence between functors from $H$ to any ordinary category and functors from $\mathcal M$ inverting $W$, including their natural transformations. Let $X,Y\in\mathcal M$, assume $X$ is cofibrant, meaning its initial map is in $C$, and $Y$ is fibrant, meaning its terminal map is in $F$. Then
$$\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal M}(X,Y)\longrightarrow\operatorname{Hom}_{H}(LX,LY),\qquad f\longmapsto L(f),$$
is surjective. No functorial factorization, enrichment or properness assumption is required.
